scenario_stem:

Its statement of financial position at 30 September shows non-current assets of $240,000, mainly a workshop lease and machinery. Current assets are $112,000, comprising inventories of $52,000, trade receivables of $38,000 and cash of $22,000. Current liabilities are $64,000, including trade payables and unpaid wages.

Kelbeck owes a bank loan of $110,000 repayable after more than one year, and shareholders' equity is $178,000. A new CNC cutting machine costing $90,000 would let Kelbeck accept larger contracts. The directors must choose between borrowing $90,000 from the bank now or waiting two years and buying it from accumulated retained profits.

scenario_stem:
Wentworth Sports Ltd is a private limited company in Country X running 5 sports goods stores in large retail parks. It employs 64 staff and revenue last year was $5.6 million from rugby, cricket and athletics equipment. Its statement of financial position at 31 January shows non-current assets of $900,000 and current assets of $680,000, comprising inventories of $470,000, receivables of $60,000 and cash of $150,000.

Current liabilities are $390,000, including $310,000 bank overdraft. It has no non-current liabilities. Share capital is $600,000 and retained profit is $590,000. The two founding shareholders both work full-time in the business. The directors must decide between paying a dividend of $100,000 to them or retaining it to refurbish the stores with new displays and lighting.

Reason 2: To judge whether a dividend is safe [k], because the bank overdraft of $310,000 inside current liabilities of $390,000 compares with cash of only $150,000 [app].

Benefit 2: They can detect over-reliance on short-term debt [k], because the bank overdraft of $310,000 lifts current liabilities to $390,000 against current assets of $680,000 [app], warning that trading cash services the overdraft instead of patient capital [an].

analysis_max_2: rising retained profit shows the business can fund itself internally

questions.question_text: Do you think Wentworth Sports Ltd should pay the $100,000 dividend or retain it to refurbish the stores? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Paying the dividend would reward the two founders [k], because share capital of $600,000 and retained profit of $590,000 show investors expect a return [app], keeping them committed to remain shareholders [an]. Refurbishing the stores could lift sales [k], because inventories of $470,000 and revenue of $5.6 million depend on fresh, appealing stores [app], and current assets of $680,000 leave only $290,000 of working capital after current liabilities of $390,000 [an]. Overall, Wentworth should retain the $100,000 [eval], because refurbishing 5 stores could raise revenue while the $310,000 overdraft needs clearing first, although a small dividend can be paid next year [eval].

scenario_stem:
Driftnet Seafoods Ltd is a private limited company in Country X processing frozen fish for 3 export buyers. It employs 96 workers and revenue last year was $8.9 million. Its statement of financial position at 31 July shows non-current assets of $1,700,000 and current assets of $1,050,000, comprising inventories of $540,000, receivables of $310,000 and cash of $200,000.

Current liabilities are $610,000. A government agency offered a $500,000 order if Driftnet files audited accounts for the last 2 years and expands cold storage by $350,000. Share capital is $1,000,000 and retained profit is $740,000, with a bank loan of $400,000 repayable after more than one year. The directors must decide whether to accept the government contract or keep serving the 3 existing buyers.

Reason 2: To confirm the firm meets its legal duties [k], because audited accounts prove that current liabilities of $610,000 and a bank loan of $400,000 are being serviced [app].

questions.question_text: Do you think Driftnet Seafoods Ltd should accept the $500,000 government contract? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Accepting would secure a big, reliable buyer [k], because existing revenue is $8.9 million from just 3 export buyers and the $500,000 order is government-backed [app], reducing dependence on a narrow customer base [an]. However, accepting means spending $350,000 on cold storage [k], because cash is only $200,000 and current liabilities of $610,000 sit against current assets of $1,050,000 [app], so Driftnet may need to borrow, straining finances if the government pays slowly [an]. Overall, Driftnet should accept the contract but negotiate staged payment [eval], because the $500,000 order strengthens revenue stability and equity of $1,740,000 supports the $350,000 expansion [eval].
